summary: Tested new browser-style NavTabs feature on desktop 1920x1080. All required behaviors work: nav-tabs bar appears after login, each sidebar click adds a new tab without replacing previous ones, active tab is highlighted (bg-white text-[#005F73]), clicking inactive tab switches route without reload, closing inactive tab removes it and keeps URL, closing active tab navigates to a neighbor, sidebar stays present. Reload does not persist tab list (only current path tab shown).
critical_code_review_comments: NavTabs.jsx closeTab() calls navigate() inside setTabs updater during render, producing React console warning: 'Cannot update a component (BrowserRouter) while rendering a different component (NavTabs)'. Refactor to compute the target outside the state updater and call navigate() after setTabs (e.g. via a useEffect on tabs+location, or capture next list synchronously then navigate). Not blocking, but should be fixed to avoid future strict-mode issues.

Requirement mentions 'F5 repart du tableau de bord'. Currently after F5 the browser keeps the previous URL (e.g. /stock) — only the tab list is reset. If the intent is to force redirect to '/' on hard reload, this is not implemented. Tabs list persistence itself is correctly not stored.
action_items: Fix React warning in NavTabs.closeTab (do not navigate inside setState updater).
Clarify/implement 'F5 returns to dashboard' behavior if required (currently URL is preserved by React Router).
context_for_next_testing_agent: NavTabs feature verified end-to-end on desktop. testids used: nav-tabs, nav-tab-home, nav-tab-equipements, nav-tab-interventions, nav-tab-stock, nav-tab-close-<slug>. Sidebar testid: sidebar. Only outstanding items are the React setState-in-render warning during closeTab and optional dashboard-on-F5 behavior.
